subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — defining product output rights and feedback license
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@horizon-systems.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Ariel Gomez <ariel.gomez@horizon.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA & Order Form — defining product output rights and feedback license

Ben — thanks for the call this morning. We reviewed Redwood's MSA + Order Form and attached our redlines (Horizon_redlines_v2.docx). High-level items we need aligned before procurement can move forward: 

- Output ownership: we expect explicit customer ownership of "generated outputs" (deliverables produced by the service) and a carveout that prevents vendor reuse for productization.
- Training / data use: Horizon will not allow customer content or outputs to be used to retrain any models without explicit written opt-in and commercial terms.
- Feedback license: we can provide aggregated telemetry and anonymized signals for product-quality improvements but not a general-purpose perpetual training license.

Can you confirm Redwood's positions and propose concrete language we can send to legal? We are on a tight procurement timeline (target signature by end of next week). Attached: redlines and SOC2 evidence we requested earlier.

Regards,
Jordan Price
Head of Platform Partnerships
Horizon Systems

Attachment: Horizon_redlines_v2.docx (word doc with inline redlines)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: MSA & Order Form — defining product output rights and feedback license

Team — forwarding Horizon's redlines. They pushed hard on output ownership and a near-total ban on training. Quick read and proposed position below before I reply to Jordan: 

Summary of our suggested principled approach:
- Customer owns their generated outputs by default for their internal use and productization.
- Redwood may retain and use strictly de-identified, aggregated telemetry and non-customer-specific feedback for improving platform performance (not for training on customer prompts/outputs).
- Training on customer content or outputs requires an explicit "Training Add-on" with separate commercial terms and opt-in language.
- For Dedicated / Private deployments we must support a contractual "no-training" checkbox with operational controls.

Action items I want to split: 
- Karthik: draft a short counter-language for the MSA + Order Form that preserves customer output title but carves out aggregate telemetry; explicitly prohibits model retraining without opt-in. Target by Fri 8/21 EOD.
- Marissa: weigh in on narrow vs. broad feedback license wording (we need to avoid giving a perpetual, transferable training license).
- Laura: prepare an updated OrderForm_DRAFT_v3.docx (incorporate our proposed clauses) and upload to HubSpot.

I will hold reply to Jordan until we have language; timeline is tight but we should aim to keep momentum.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA & Order Form — defining product output rights and feedback license

Ben/Karthik/Laura — thanks for the heads up. A few legal redline suggestions (short and actionable):

1) Output ownership: we can accept a clause that "Customer owns Outputs" but add narrow language that clarifies Redwood retains operational rights to tokenize/transform outputs for logging, debugging, and safety use (non-commercial). Proposed text: 
"Customer retains ownership of Outputs. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may retain and use Outputs to the extent strictly necessary to debug, monitor, and improve service reliability, provided such use is limited to non‑commercial, aggregated purposes."

2) Feedback license: counter-propose a time-limited, non-exclusive license for anonymized feedback signals only. Avoid "perpetual, transferable, royalty-free" phrasing. Suggested: 
"Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive license to use Feedback solely in anonymized and aggregated form to improve the Redwood service; such use shall not include training on Customer Content unless Customer executes a separate Training Agreement."

3) Training & PII: add a hard consent requirement — "Redwood will not use Customer Content (including Outputs) to train models unless Customer provides express written consent and executes a Training Addendum that specifies scope and compensation. Redwood will not use PII for training under any circumstances without explicit approval and redaction controls."

4) Operational segregation: for Dedicated/Private customers include an addendum checkbox: "No-training; no telemetry export outside customer's VPC" — we need engineering confirmation on feasibility.

I'll draft exact language for the MSA and a short paragraph for the Order Form. Karthik, if you can format into one redline (tracked changes) that Jordan can pass to Horizon Legal, that will speed things up.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Legal & Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@horizon-systems.com>

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — defining product output rights and feedback license

Ben / Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround and the constructive positions. Horizon is generally comfortable with the compromise language you outlined, provided: 

- Output ownership language is explicit that Horizon can productize outputs without vendor claim.
- Feedback license is strictly "anonymized, aggregated, non-train" as you propose. Add a cross-reference to our privacy section to define "anonymized" (we can provide suggested wording).
- Training add-on: acceptable to require a separate written opt-in and commercial terms.

I've attached SOC evidence for compliance questions and uploaded our final redline suggestions; I also added a few small edits to the OrderForm to reflect purchase of the Training Add-on as a separate line item.

If Redwood can accept the MSA counter-language in principle, we can route to Horizon Legal (Ariel) for final markups and then push to DocuSign. I attached a DocuSign preview for the Order Form as a convenience (link below). We are targeting signature by Friday if possible.

Regards,

Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Final path forward — output rights, feedback license, training add-on (Horizon Systems)

Team / Jordan / Ariel — thanks everyone for fast collaboration. Quick summary of agreed next steps and owners so procurement can finish: 

Agreed record (to be reflected in MSA + Order Form):
- Customer Outputs: Horizon retains exclusive right to use and productize Outputs generated from its account. Redwood retains a limited, non-commercial right to use Outputs only for debugging, safety, and aggregated reliability metrics.
- Feedback License: Redwood may use anonymized and aggregated Feedback signals for platform improvement. Feedback shall not be used to train models on identifiable Customer Content or Outputs.
- Training Use: Any use of Customer Content or Outputs to train models requires a separate Training Addendum and explicit commercial terms; default is "no-training".
- Dedicated/Private: Include a checkbox/addendum that enforces a no-telemetry, no-training mode and specifies operational constraints (engineering to validate).

Owners / due dates:
- Karthik Iyer: Draft the exact MSA clause + Order Form line for "Training Add-on" and update OrderForm_DRAFT_v3.docx — due Tue 8/25 COB.
- Marissa Cole: Finalize feedback-license wording and run with Ariel to confirm Horizon Legal's acceptance.
- Laura Bennett: Upload revised OrderForm to HubSpot and attach DocuSign preview.
- Ben Carter: Coordinate commercial (pricing for Training Add-on) and confirm timeline with Jordan; I'll chase signature target Friday if redlines are accepted.

Jordan — from Horizon's side, please confirm that the proposed clarifying language above accurately reflects Horizon's view; if so, we'll push the draft to Ariel for final markups and get the DocuSign in motion.

Thanks — moving quickly on this will keep the Q3 deployment timeline intact.

—Ben
Ben Carter
